title: Intrinsic randomness generation makes large-scale behavior stable

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Intrinsic randomness generation makes large-scale behavior stable

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Systems that intrinsically generate randomness, like rule 22 or rule 30, produce the same overall random behavior with the same large-scale properties whatever their initial conditions, giving them a fundamental stability that he says underlies the apparent stability of many systems in nature.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: By intrinsically generating randomness such systems in a sense have a certain fundamental stability: for whatever is done to their initial conditions, they still give the same overall random behavior, with the same large-scale properties.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Special Initial Conditions” (from p. 266), p. 266. Scope: intrinsically random cellular automata and natural systems with apparent stability

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.60

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Robustness over large ensembles of initial states is easy to test computationally. The universal qualifier and extrapolation to nature cannot be resolved without narrowing the systems and stability variables.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For rules 22 and 30, sample broad families of initial conditions and compare asymptotic densities, correlations, entropy rates, and coarse-grained distributions. Separately test whether analogous invariant statistics predict stability in named natural systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Simulation similarity does not establish the natural mechanism.

Exceptional initial conditions contradict a literal “whatever.”

Large-scale properties and natural systems are unspecified.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Stability of coarse statistics for rule 22 and rule 30 is a straightforward simulation and can be confirmed or challenged on those rules. The sentence then says this kind of stability underlies the apparent stability of many natural systems, which requires observations the automaton survey does not contain. The computational half is in reach; the explanatory half is not resolved by it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare block statistics of rule 22 and rule 30 across widely different seeds, looking for stable densities and entropies despite sensitive details. Matching large-scale statistics support the automaton half; the natural-systems half needs a named phenomenon and a perturbation test that existing automaton runs do not provide.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Stable averages are also produced by noisy systems that do not generate randomness intrinsically.

The natural-systems clause names no phenomenon and no dataset.

Which large-scale properties must match is not fixed.

operationalizability: 0.55
